contexts.text: The feasts which were made in the evening, or suppers, among the Ancients... signified nothing else than the state of initiation which precedes conjunction, which state is relatively obscure. Explained.
Under Passover, see this reference. AC 7997. AC 8001.
Hence meat and drink nourish the body better... when a man at his supper or dinner is at the same time in the delight of conversing with others about such things as he loves. Explained.
That the spiritual sense of the Word will be opened at the end of the Church, is signified... also by the Great Supper () DSS 25. TCR 207.
I will sup with him, and he with Me () = that the Lord conjoins Himself with them, and them with Himself. ( = a communication to them of the happinesses of Heaven. AE 252.)

It is said to sup, and the Lord's Supper, because supper takes place in the evening, and by the evening is signified the last time of the Church; and therefore when the Lord went away out of the world, it being then the last time of the Church, He supped with His disciples, and instituted the Sacrament of the Supper. AR 816:end.

Blessed are they who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb () = ... that there is eternal life for those who receive the things which are of the Lord's New Church. ( = that those will come into Heaven who are conjoined with the Lord through truths from the Word, and that they become of the Church. AE 1225.)

The reason it is called the marriage supper of the Lamb, is that this happens in the last state of the Church, which is called evening, and suppers take place in the evening. In the evening, man is called to the Church, and, when those who have been called are present, it is morning.
Come, and gather yourselves together to the supper of the Great God () = the Lord... convoking... to the New Church, and to conjunction with Himself, and thus to eternal life.
They supped with that privy-councillor; and, after supper, they... separated, each to his own bedroom.
That the diversions of charity are suppers, etc.

In the Primitive Church... suppers signified consociations and conjunctions in the first state of the establishment of the Church; for evening, when they took place, signified this state. (Continued. See Dinner.)
When it is time for dinner, and also for supper, a table appears with food; and it disappears when they have dined or supped. LJPost 331.
Mention is made of supping, because weddings look place when there were suppers...
As suppers = consociations by love, and the communication of delights then, the Lord compared the Church and Heaven to a supper, and also to weddings. Illustrated.
Heaven and the Church as to spiritual nourishment, that is, instruction, are signified by the great supper to which they were invited (). (Compare AE 695:6.)
A supper = consociation by love, and communication.
